exercise.name: Cable Half Kneeling Pallof Press

reference.title: Cable Half Kneeling Pallof Press
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (half-kneeling side-on to a chest-height pulley, press out and hold square).

exercise.mechanics: Isometric trunk (anti-rotation) with a horizontal press

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you press, breathe steadily through the hold, in as the hands come back.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s out, 1.5 s hold, 1 s back

prescription.load: User-chosen: the cable should pull hard but never twist you
prescription.progression: Longer holds, then more weight, then tall kneeling or standing with the feet together

cues.text: Half-kneel side-on to the pulley, inside knee down, front foot flat; hold the handle with both hands at the middle of the chest.
Press straight out from the chest; do not let the cable turn you.
Hold at arm's length: hips and shoulders square to the front, glute of the down leg tight.
Bring the handle back to the chest, still square.

mistakes.fix: Lighter weight; brace and squeeze the glute of the down leg.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning or arching away from the cable
mistakes.fix: Stay tall, ribs down, pelvis level.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing up instead of straight out
mistakes.fix: The hands travel level with the chest.
Keep the front shin vertical and the knee over the foot.

kinematics.norm: None: resist the cable's turning pull (anti-rotation; clinical opinion)
From the chest straight out to about arm's length at chest height (clinical opinion)
Bent at the chest, nearly straight at the end (clinical opinion)
Half-kneeling narrows the base and takes the legs out of the bracing (clinical opinion); unilateral loading raises trunk activity (Saeterbakken 2012)
Slow press, hold of a few seconds (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #14486, Cable Half Kneeling Pallof Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Knee pain on the down knee: use a thicker pad or switch to the standing version.
Choose a load you can hold square; the load is user-chosen.
Low-back pain: keep the ribs down and the pelvis level.
modify: Standing Pallof press with the feet wider.
regressions: Shorter holds with the hands closer to the chest.
progressions: Pallof press with an overhead reach.

muscleNotes.obliques_l: The obliques on both sides stop the trunk turning toward the pulley; the far-side internal and near-side external obliques work hardest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Work with the other side to hold the trunk square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and the deep abdominals brace the trunk; McGill 1998 describes this kind of bracing for spine stability.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Presses the hands out and holds them there (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Presses the hands out and holds them there (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Helps press the handle out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Helps press the handle out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Reaches the shoulder blades forward at the end of the press (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Reaches the shoulder blades forward at the end of the press (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: The down-leg glute keeps the hip extended and the pelvis square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steadies the pelvis on the narrow base (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Steadies the pelvis on the narrow base (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blades steady against the sideways pull (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Hold the shoulder blades steady against the sideways pull (clinical opinion).
